calls.head: Iron sharpens iron
calls.body: The Hurricanes are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Blues are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Hurricanes’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Hurricanes’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Blues.

calls.head: Power vs. Power
calls.body: At home, the Blues keep sending Thomas’s line (Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Montgomery has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Hurricanes’ first line is Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.
calls.call: The Blues’ L1 (Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud) spends at least 44% of its 5-on-5 time against the Hurricanes’ first line, against about 31% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 57% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 31% with no line matching

calls.plain: St. Louis sent Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud out against the Hurricanes’ first line for 57% of their 5-on-5 time, far more than the 31% they’d get with no line matching.

STL.head: We had St. Louis as slight underdogs (43%), and it went Carolina’s way.

CAR.head: We leaned Carolina’s way (57%), and they came through.

surprises.head: St. Louis couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: St. Louis usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots, and Carolina usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: St. Louis’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 5.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.9% (about 7.7% against Carolina) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: A shutout for Pyotr Kochetkov
surprises.body: Kochetkov stopped all 24 shots, worth 2.1 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 15 starts.

story.head: Kochetkov shuts out the Blues
paras: Sean Walker and Jesperi Kotkaniemi scored just 20 seconds apart early in the second to put the Hurricanes up 2-0. Logan Stankoven made it 3-0 midway through the period, and Nikolaj Ehlers stretched the lead to 4-0 on the power play early in the third.

The Hurricanes carried the play, outshooting the Blues 39-24, and got the result to match. Pyotr Kochetkov was perfect for the Canes, 24 saves on 24 shots, and Joel Hofer stopped 35 of 39 at the other end. Kochetkov has won all seven of his starts this season.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Hurricanes moved to 9-2-2, still first in the NHL in points, while the Blues fell to 5-5-1, slipping to sixth in the Central.
